A controlled reset-based retest (CONDITION run -> RENEW run, no reset between) did NOT reproduce the leak (RENEW's conditions came back empty and ALLOW). classification_reason: In one un-reset run sequence a RENEW run surfaced a stale approvedChangeTicket condition-requirement and a validity-output that still read PASS despite technical-validity being set to FAIL; a controlled CONDITION-then-RENEW retest without reset did not reproduce this. SOURCE REVIEW NOTE: data/scenarios/privileged-system-access.json's ui.dispositionTemplates shows the 'conditions' array (the approvedChangeTicket predicate) is declared exclusively inside the CONDITION template, with no shared/global condition object referenced by RENEW's template -- so the static configuration does not itself explain a leak into RENEW. This rules out a config-level design flaw as the cause and narrows the hypothesis to a live client-side state-management artifact (e.g. an incomplete object reset when the disposition dropdown changes), consistent with the 'REVIEW REQUIRED, not confirmed' framing rather than a confirmed defect.
